name: Nuria: typed sparse JSON Patch
hypothesis: Direct scalar comparisons and a single mapping traversal avoid repeated JSON encoding on mostly unchanged snapshots. Prefix/suffix trimming handles common list appends and deletions. A bounded size check replaces operation-heavy subtrees when replacement is substantially smaller. This could reduce encoding time, but the timing and compressed-size targets require measurement. The reported correctness failure is fixed by distinguishing integers from floats; signed floating-point zero is also preserved.
tradeoffs: Produces only RFC 6902 add/remove/replace operations, escapes pointer tokens, and never mutates either snapshot.
Fallback performs at most four subtree-size comparisons. Its raw-size heuristic does not guarantee smaller gzip output or bound the cost of generating the initial patch.
No move detection or general list alignment: multiple interior insertions and reordering can produce larger patches.
Recursive traversal is subject to Python's recursion limit. Operation values reference the immutable new snapshot.
Validate strict reconstruction and measure server encoding, gzip bytes, and client application against both baselines; no performance result is claimed here.
